title: Why I'm Doubling Down on This Hated Stock
summary: Couch Investor defends two 'hated' names — Meta and SoFi — arguing broken stocks, not broken businesses. On compute: yes, more is needed, but newer models and GPUs are getting far more efficient (Nvidia's Vera Rubin: 30% better throughput per megawatt), and much inference waste comes from using frontier models for simple tasks. He notes Codex grew from 6M to 25M weekly users in ~25 weeks and OpenAI's ad business is nearing $1B ARR. The bulk is Meta: Zuckerberg's promotion of Muse Code out of beta, insanely cheap pricing ($5/month tiers), a power move to maximize adoption and harvest usage data to improve models. He cites Bernstein: Meta could overtake Google Search as the largest ad-dollar destination before year-end, having captured nearly half of every incremental digital ad dollar in 2026 with ~20.4% ad growth. Personal AI agents launching across 3B+ users could monetize via take rates — but must be sticky versus Anthropic, OpenAI, Grok, and Gemini. He likens Meta today to Google in 2025 and muses about $1,000/share by end of 2027. Also covered: Anthropic's $35B Lambda (Nvidia-backed) cloud deal plus a $45B Nscale deal; IREN/Hut 8 speculation. On SoFi: the stock is -35% YTD but guidance was raised despite worse rate assumptions, his DCF still expects ~30% revenue growth through 2028 and rising EBIT margins — execution is strong, sentiment is not. Calls: META HOLD; SOFI HOLD.
